content.text: Most tutorials about [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/building-crypto-store-cloudflare-pages-everything-you-need-2|building]] a digital store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most creators get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/why-payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-only-real|COREMERCH guide to payment]]s webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-works-how-2|How Supabase]] for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOWPayments second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to this infrastructure's success lies in its sovereignty. By using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, you're building a digital store that's completely independent of any single platform. This means you're not subject to platform restrictions, and you have full ownership of your store and its data from day one.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store on Cloudflare Pages, you'll need to set up a few essential components. First, you'll need to create a GitHub Pages site or a Cloudflare Pages project. Next, you'll need to configure your payment and delivery pipeline using NOWPayments and Google Cloud Storage or Cloudflare R2. Finally, you'll need to create a Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or an Edge Commerce Stack ($197) on the COREMERCH website.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The NOWPayments configuration sequence is the same regardless of which stack you are deploying. Create a NOWPayments account — no KYC required, no document upload, no bank account needed. Navigate to the wallet settings and add the wallet addresses for each cryptocurrency you want to accept. USDT on Tron and Bitcoin are the practical starting point for most creators in restricted markets. Generate an API key from the NOWPayments dashboard. Set the webhook endpoint URL in the NOWPayments IPN settings pointing to your Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App. Set the webhook secret key — a string you generate that both NOWPayments and your backend know.
Deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages for free requires a Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or an Edge Commerce Stack ($197) on the COREMERCH website.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.

If you're looking to scale your digital store, consider upgrading to the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which provides advanced features like SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration and end-to-end testing. Additionally, you can explore other products on the COREMERCH website, such as the Sovereign Blueprint ($47) or the Complete Builder Kit ($197), to help you get started with your digital store.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your digital store on Cloudflare Pages, follow these steps: Create a GitHub Pages site or a Cloudflare Pages project, configure your payment and delivery pipeline using NOWPayments and Google Cloud Storage or Cloudflare R2, create a Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or an Edge Commerce Stack ($197) on the COREMERCH website, deploy your stack in 4-6 hours or less, and test your store on mainnet before going live.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 in COREMERCH?

Stack 01 is a basic infrastructure stack that provides a digital store with automatic crypto payment processing, instant product delivery, and full data ownership. Stack 02, on the other hand, is an advanced infrastructure stack that provides additional features like SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support.
Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?

Yes, you can host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. These platforms provide a free and secure way to host your digital store, and can be used in conjunction with other infrastructure components like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script.
How do I test my digital store on mainnet before going live?

To test your digital store on mainnet before going live, follow the instructions provided by COREMERCH to deploy your stack, then use the NOWPayments dashboard to set up a test payment and verify that it is processed correctly.
